Update this weekly digest to Week 5. Make exactly these four changes and nothing else. STEP 1 - STATUS LINE. The bold status line directly under the document title must read exactly: Week 5 · 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-08 · Phase: Pre-production Leave the smaller grey line beneath it unchanged. STEP 2 - the bullet list in the 'What changed' section. Replace that
    element with exactly this HTML, character for character:
    • Perforce to Git LFS migration completed for the audio depot
    • Grapple traversal prototype playable end to end on the test level
    STEP 3 - the 'What is at risk' table. Replace the ENTIRE contents of that table's with exactly these 2 rows, character for character. Keep its header row exactly as it is: Boss encounter difficulty untuned for controllerAna F.DesignLowworseningOutsourced character art slipping two weeksPriya N.ArtLowsteady STEP 4 - the bullet list in the 'What is next' section. Replace that
      element with exactly this HTML, character for character:
      • Stand up the automated build farm
      • Decide Wwise vs FMOD
      Do not touch the 'Archive' section at all. REPLACEMENT MEANS REPLACEMENT: where this instruction lists what a section must contain, the section must end up containing exactly that and nothing else. Delete what is not on the list rather than keeping it alongside. Preserve all existing formatting exactly: the document title, every section heading, table borders, header-row shading, alternating row colours, fonts, font sizes and colours. Do not restyle anything. Do not add, remove or rename any heading. Do not reorder the sections. Copy every quoted or listed value character for character. Do not add a full stop to a bullet that has none, and do not reword anything. STRUCTURAL RULE: both tables must remain elements with their header rows intact. Never replace a table with a single row, a div or a list. Never drop a table's header row.

Nebula Drift - Weekly Production Digest

Week 5 · 2026-02-02 to 2026-02-08 · Phase: Pre-production
Vantage Nine Studios · internal · standing document, edited in place every Monday

What changed

  • Perforce to Git LFS migration completed for the audio depot
  • Grapple traversal prototype playable end to end on the test level

What is at risk

RiskOwnerArea SeverityTrend
Boss encounter difficulty untuned for controllerAna F.DesignLowworsening
Outsourced character art slipping two weeksPriya N.ArtLowsteady

What is next

  • Lock the art direction to one of the two candidates
  • Scope the vertical slice level list

Archive

Newest first. Detail rows older than 8 weeks are folded into a single rolled-up row so this section stays readable at 52 weeks.

Week Dates Shipped Risks carried
Week 4 2026-01-26 to 2026-02-01 Drift Belt nav-mesh and Salvage economy spreadsheet first pass. Nav-mesh generation for the Drift Belt sector; First pass on the Salvage economy spreadsheet Boss encounter difficulty and outsourced character art slipping. Boss encounter difficulty untuned for controller; Outsourced character art slipping two weeks
Week 3 2026-01-19 to 2026-01-25 Core loop pitch deck signed off by publisher; engine upgrade merged; build times down 31%; art style narrowed; nav-mesh generated. Boss encounter difficulty untuned for controller; outsourced character art slipping two weeks. Boss encounter difficulty untuned for controller; outsourced character art slipping two weeks.
Week 2 2026-01-12 to 2026-01-18 Second combat designer hired, starts week 9; audio depot migrated to Git LFS; grapple traversal prototype playable on test level Save-game format unversioned; boss encounter difficulty untuned for controller; outsourced character art slipping two weeks
Week 1 2026-01-05 to 2026-01-11 Art style exploration narrowed to two directions; nav-mesh generation for Drift Belt sector Save-game format still unversioned; boss encounter difficulty untuned for controller; outsourced character art slipping two weeks.
